I will do it much like last year, with small adjustments if the price of fertilizer jumps. On my 10.7 mu, the land does not rest because I do wheat and maize one after the other, so I will keep the whole 10.7 mu in both crops. I farm the way I have seen work around me. If the field looks hungry, I would rather put a bit more fertilizer than let the crop go yellow and lose grain. Wheat matters because it carries us through the year, and maize matters because if the ears do not fill, the money drops fast. Since I have well water, I will not let the crop suffer dry spells if I can help it. For wheat, I will use the usual improved seed people around here trust, put a heavier base fertilizer, water it about 3 times, spray about 2 times, and aim for a steady harvest. For maize, I will use hybrid seed like most people do now, keep fertilizer a little lower than wheat but still enough to hold yield, water about 2 times if rain is short, spray about 2 times, and use rotary tillage after wheat so I can turn around fast. I do not like gambling on big changes, so I will follow the path I know, keep costs in line, and make sure neither crop goes short on fertilizer or water.
